newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINA SEES $8-9 BLN 1997 CURRENT ACCOUNT GAP.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINA SEES $8-9 BLN 1997 CURRENT ACCOUNT GAP.

text.p: The Argentine government's Economic Policy Secretary, Carlos Rodriguez, said Wednesday he expected the current account deficit for 1997 to be between $8-9 billion.
A $9 billion deficit would be equivalent to 2.8 percent of Argentina's gross domestic product, an increase of almost one percentage point on the 1996 deficit.

But Rodriguez told reporters such a deficit would not be worrying as it results from the inflow of capital. He added that 45 percent of the deficit was accounted for by imports of capital goods as a result of Argentina's high economic growth.
"It confirms that the current account deficit is the flip side of the entry of capital," said Rodriguez, the second highest official in the Economy Ministry.
